Distinction of claim scope among Nimbus incident review statements.

The network team statement (block 58) disputes that an upstream network fault initiated the
checkout errors. This characterization does not appear as an asserted claim in the other
responding blocks: the database team (57) attributes observed effects to retry amplification
following a routing change without claiming an upstream network fault, and the checkout
application team (59) hypothesizes a malformed routing rule concentrating traffic on one pool.
The timeline (56) does not assign a single root cause. The network team's dispute may therefore
address a characterization of the routing change itself (whether it qualifies as a network
fault) or a claim external to these four blocks.

Official Nimbus payments incident timeline, 2025-06-04.

At 09:12 UTC checkout errors rose after a routing change. The team rolled back routing at 09:31,
and error rates returned to baseline by 09:38. The timeline does not assign a single root cause.

Database team observation for the Nimbus incident review.

Connection wait time rose sharply at 09:14 UTC, two minutes after the routing change. The team
believes retry amplification contributed, but cannot determine whether it initiated the failure.

Network team statement for the Nimbus incident review.

Packet loss remained within the normal range throughout the incident. The team disputes the claim
that an upstream network fault initiated the checkout errors.

Checkout application team hypothesis, written before load replay.

A malformed routing rule may have concentrated traffic on one pool and triggered database retry
amplification. This is a working explanation, not a confirmed causal conclusion.
